Compute NFL Clinching and Elimination Status

Source: R/clinching_status.R
nfl_clinching_status.Rd

Determine for every team whether it has clinched, can still reach, or has been eliminated from a division title, a playoff berth and the No. 1 seed, given the games played so far.

Usage

nfl_clinching_status(
  games,
  ...,
  status = c("DIV", "PLAYOFFS", "1SEED"),
  scenarios = FALSE,
  search = FALSE,
  verbosity = c("MIN", "MAX", "NONE")
)

Arguments

games

A data frame of played and remaining games, like nflreadr::load_schedules(). It needs the variables sim or season, game_type, week, away_team, home_team and result (see nfl_standings()). Games with a result are played, regular season games with result = NA are still to be played. To get the status after a given week, set result of all later games to NA.

Cancelled games must be removed from games, otherwise they count as games still to be played.

...

currently not used

status

One or more of "DIV", "PLAYOFFS" and "1SEED": the goals to compute.

  • "DIV": win the division.

  • "PLAYOFFS": make the playoffs, as division winner or wild card.

  • "1SEED": be the No. 1 seed of the conference.

Only the requested goals are computed. "PLAYOFFS" takes the most time.

scenarios

If TRUE, the result gets the attribute "scenarios", the results of the remaining games that prove the answers (see Value).

search

If TRUE, answers the proofs leave open are searched by fixing the results of remaining games one at a time, within a fixed budget (see Details). This decides more teams but takes more time, mostly with many games left. With FALSE (default), the function says how many statuses are "undecided" and whether the search might help.

verbosity

One of "MIN", "MAX", or "NONE".

  • "MIN" (default): Prints the main steps.

  • "MAX": Also prints all steps of the tiebreaking process of the current standings and how many teams got each status.

  • "NONE": No status reports.

Value

The current standings: the output of nfl_standings() for the games played so far (with conference ranks and tiebreakers through strength of schedule), followed by games_left (regular season games still to be played) and one status column per requested goal: div_status, playoffs_status and seed1_status. Each status is one of "clinched", "alive", "eliminated" or "undecided". Like nfl_standings(), there is only a row for teams that have played at least one game, and the rows are sorted the same way.

With scenarios = TRUE, the attribute "scenarios" is a data.table with one row per scenario and remaining game of its season: scenario (an id), season (or sim), team, goal ("DIV", "PLAYOFFS" or "1SEED"), proves ("reach" or "miss": the team reaches or misses the goal with these results), coin_toss (TRUE if it does so only with a particular coin toss), followed by the columns of games with the results of the scenario. Played games together with the rows of one scenario can go straight into nfl_standings(). Seasons without remaining games have no rows.

Details

For every goal, the function answers two questions: can the team still reach the goal, and can it still miss it, over all possible results (win, loss or tie) of the remaining games. The status follows from the answers:

Can reachCan missStatus
noyes"eliminated"
yesno"clinched"
yesyes"alive"
not proven"undecided"

Every answer is proven, either by showing that no results of the remaining games can do it, or by a concrete set of results run through the standings (see scenarios). Where tiebreakers decide, the function goes through the ways the teams of the conference can end above, level with or below the team, and proves who wins each of these ties. It never tries every combination of results, so a few teams can be "undecided" when the answer depends on tiebreakers it can't settle in advance.

With search = TRUE, an open answer is searched further: the function fixes the result of one remaining game at a time (home win, away win, tie) and proves the answer for each case, up to 200 cases per answer. This helps most with 5 or fewer games left per team.

Tiebreakers through strength of schedule are applied as in nfl_standings(). Coin tosses and tiebreakers based on points can't be known before they happen, so both of their outcomes count as possible. A goal that only a coin toss decides after the last game is "undecided".

Seasons through 2019 have 6 playoff seeds per conference, later seasons 7. With sim instead of season, 7 seeds are used.

With a single season in games, the function puts more effort into ties of many teams (mostly for the No. 1 seed with many games left), which can take a few seconds. With more than one season, e.g. simulated seasons, it gives up on them earlier, so more statuses are "undecided".

The results are compared with the official clinching flags of the NFL for every week of 2006 to 2025, one season at a time: no status contradicts them, and every team clinches or is eliminated in the same week as in the NFL, with and without search.

See also

For the implemented tiebreakers, see https://nflseedr.com/articles/tiebreaker.html

Examples

# \donttest{
try({#to avoid CRAN test problems
  games <- nflreadr::load_schedules(2023)
})
# Status after week 15
games$result[games$week > 15] <- NA
status <- nflseedR::nfl_clinching_status(games)
